title: Country-level immunization recovery and DTP1 no-dose proxy burden after COVID-19: a descriptive ecological analysis of WUENIC, 2010-2024.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review examines country-level immunization recovery and DTP1 no-dose proxy burden after COVID-19, focusing on access, series completion, measles coverage, and recovery from 2019 across 194 countries/reporting entities during 2010-2024.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A descriptive ecological analysis using exact-2024-revision WHO/UNICEF WUENIC records, with estimation of recovery, DTP1 no-dose burden, DTP3-MCV1 overlap, and phenotype assignments. Benchmarks were reproduced, and sensitivity analyses included source-status, target-population-weighted, threshold, and exact-2025-revision approaches.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Aggregate immunization coverage in 2024 was near 2019 levels (DTP1: 88.94%, DTP3: 84.56%, MCV1: 84.03%), but country-level fixed-effects estimates showed declines (-1.80 to -2.09 percentage points). The DTP1 no-dose proxy burden was 14.26 million, with the top 20 entities accounting for 74.6%, and 45 entities with low DTP3/Measles coverage representing 72.8% of the burden.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Threshold changes reassigned at most 13.4% of entities, and 2025 data revisions altered 20 recovery-class and 19 phenotype assignments among 194 common entities. Assignments are descriptive and revision-specific, not validated risk scores, and may not fully capture nuanced recovery patterns.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Program managers should jointly review entity-level signals for access, completion, measles coverage, recovery, and data quality rather than relying on single rankings. Descriptive phenotypes require contextual interpretation and should not be used as standalone risk metrics.

analysis.summary_en: This ecological analysis of WHO/UNICEF WUENIC data (2010-2024) reveals that while global immunization coverage rebounded to near-2019 levels by 2024, significant country-level disparities persist. DTP1 no-dose proxy burden reached 14.26 million, concentrated in 45 low-coverage entities. Fixed-effects estimates showed declines in DTP1, DTP3, and MCV1 coverage from 2019 to 2024. Phenotype assignments are descriptive and revision-specific, requiring joint interpretation of multiple signals rather than single rankings. Program managers must prioritize context-specific recovery strategies and avoid over-reliance on aggregate metrics.

title: Tunable Immune Imprinting of Memory B Cells to SARS-CoV-2 Variants 2255300

analysis.research_question_and_background: Immune imprinting biases memory B cell recall toward ancestral strains, limiting vaccine adaptability to evolving variants, and whether this imprinting can be modulated by host immune factors remains unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We recruited tightly time-matched cohorts of healthy individuals and SLE patients who had received three doses of ancestral inactivated vaccine and subsequently experienced synchronized Omicron BA.5/BF.7 breakthrough infection.
analysis.methods: We characterized their MBC responses through monoclonal antibody (mAb) epitope mapping, deep mutational scanning (DMS), spectral flow cytometry, and antigen-linked single-cell multi-omics.
analysis.main_results: Healthy individuals displayed strong immune imprinting with robust recall of high-affinity cross-reactive MBCs, while SLE patients exhibited markedly reduced imprinting with enhanced recognition of variant-specific neutralizing epitopes and attenuated MBC recall.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Our findings demonstrate that immune imprinting in MBCs is plastic, and modulation of inflammatory and B cell activation signaling can rebalance recall versus de novo responses to promote variant-adaptable immunity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These insights suggest that targeting inflammatory pathways could enhance vaccine responses against evolving variants, potentially informing strategies to improve COVID-19 vaccine adaptability.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence strength is moderate, as it is based on abstract-only data without detailed methods or statistical analyses, limiting assessment of generalizability and potential biases.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated immune imprinting in memory B cells (MBCs) following SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and breakthrough infection. Researchers compared healthy individuals and SLE patients, finding that SLE patients exhibited reduced immune imprinting and enhanced recognition of variant-specific epitopes. The results demonstrate that immune imprinting is plastic and can be modulated by host inflammatory factors, offering insights for improving vaccine adaptability against evolving variants.

title: Immunogenicity, reactogenicity, and safety of an mRNA-based seasonal influenza and SARS-CoV-2 multicomponent vaccine, mRNA-1083, in adults aged ≥50 years in Japan.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health need for simplified seasonal vaccination by evaluating whether a single mRNA-based multicomponent vaccine could provide simultaneous protection against seasonal influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in adults aged ≥50 years.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A phase 3, Asia-Pacific, randomized, observer-blind trial (Part 1 in Japan) enrolled adults aged ≥50 years who were randomized 1:1 to receive mRNA-1083 plus placebo or licensed influenza HA vaccine plus mRNA-1273, with 2022 participants randomized and 2013 receiving study intervention.
analysis.methods: Participants received either mRNA-1083 or active comparators; immunogenicity was assessed at Day 29 and Day 181, and safety/reactogenicity were monitored throughout, including solicited adverse reactions and serious adverse events.
analysis.main_results: At Day 29, mRNA-1083 elicited noninferior immune responses versus active comparators for all evaluated influenza strains and SARS-CoV-2, with superiority demonstrated for comparator-matched influenza strains and SARS-CoV-2 in the overall population.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as demonstrating that mRNA-1083 can provide simultaneous protection against influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in a single injection, representing a novel approach to seasonal vaccination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results support mRNA-1083 as a potential single-dose seasonal vaccination strategy against influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in adults aged ≥50 years, with immune responses maintained through 6 months post-vaccination.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a single phase 3 trial in Japan with short-term follow-up; generalizability to other populations and long-term safety requires further study, warranting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This phase 3, randomized, observer-blind trial in Japan evaluated the immunogenicity, reactogenicity, and safety of the mRNA-based multicomponent vaccine mRNA-1083, which combines seasonal influenza and SARS-CoV-2 antigens, in adults aged ≥50 years. At Day 29, mRNA-1083 elicited noninferior immune responses versus active comparators for all evaluated influenza strains and SARS-CoV-2, with superiority observed for comparator-matched influenza strains and SARS-CoV-2 in the overall population. Immune responses remained above baseline and comparable to or numerically higher than active comparators at Day 181. The vaccine demonstrated an acceptable safety profile, with most solicited adverse reactions being grade 1 or 2, no cases of myocarditis or pericarditis, and no related serious adverse events or deaths. These findings support mRNA-1083 as a single-dose approach to seasonal vaccination against influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in adults ≥50 years, though generalizability and long-term safety require further study.

title: Estimating Time-Inhomogeneous Transition Probabilities from District Level Daily COVID-19 Transmission Data in Sierra Leone

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the limitation of conventional compartmental epidemic models that assume fixed transition probabilities between disease states, which does not reflect the dynamic reality of COVID-19 transmission influenced by interventions and variants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This paper develops a time-inhomogeneous Markov chain framework for the SEIR process and applies it to a compiled daily, district-level COVID-19 surveillance panel for Sierra Leone spanning March 2020 to December 2023, covering 16 districts and 1,401 days.
analysis.methods: The study derives a constrained maximum likelihood estimator for time-varying transition probabilities, establishes its statistical properties, and proposes a stochastic machine learning hybrid extension that regresses smoothed probabilities on policy and mobility covariates using logistic regression and random forest.
analysis.main_results: The likelihood ratio test rejects time-homogeneity of the exposed-to-infectious transition in 15 of 16 districts and the infectious-to-removed transition in 8 of 16 districts (α = 0.05), and the covariate-augmented logistic model achieves an out-of-sample Brier score roughly 76 times smaller than a time-homogeneous baseline.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these results as statistical evidence that time-inhomogeneous, covariate-informed Markov models provide a materially better description of district-level COVID-19 transmission in Sierra Leone than classical time-homogeneous models.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have implications for sub-national outbreak monitoring in resource-constrained settings, demonstrating the value of dynamic models that incorporate real-world interventions and mobility data.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is high, as the study uses a large, comprehensive dataset and rigorous statistical methods, though limitations may include potential unmeasured confounders not captured in the covariates.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the limitation of conventional epidemic models by developing a time-inhomogeneous Markov chain framework for COVID-19 transmission. Applied to district-level data from Sierra Leone (March 2020-December 2023), the framework allows transition probabilities to vary over time while respecting SEIR structural constraints. The likelihood ratio test rejects time-homogeneity in most districts, and a covariate-augmented model significantly outperforms a homogeneous baseline. Healthcare capacity and time trends emerged as key predictors. The findings demonstrate that dynamic, covariate-informed models better capture real-world transmission dynamics, offering valuable insights for outbreak monitoring in resource-limited settings.

title: Recovery of proofreading-impaired SARS-CoV-2 reveals a mutator phenotype and an ExoN activity threshold for viability.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed whether SARS-CoV-2 can tolerate impaired proofreading activity by its ExoN enzyme, as previous research suggested complete inactivation is lethal, leaving unresolved the virus's capacity for partial proofreading impairment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research employed a continuous fluorescence-based biochemical assay combined with an optimized single-bacmid reverse genetics system to investigate the functional requirement for ExoN in SARS-CoV-2 replication.
analysis.methods: Mutational analysis of residues involved in RNA binding or catalysis was performed, with ExoN activity assessed in vitro, and recombinant SARS-CoV-2 mutants were recovered and evaluated for replication capacity and genome-wide sequence variation via deep sequencing.
analysis.main_results: Mutational analysis revealed graded effects on ExoN activity, with the K9A mutant showing no activity reduction and being readily recovered, the D90A/E92A mutant exhibiting reduced activity and delayed recovery but maintaining substitutions during serial passage, and the K9E mutant being unrecoverable despite repeated attempts; the D90A/E92A mutant displayed a stable mutator phenotype with increased genome-wide sequence variation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that SARS-CoV-2 can tolerate substantial impairment of ExoN activity but depends on a minimal activity threshold for viability, demonstrating a mutator phenotype when proofreading is partially compromised.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This research clarifies how coronavirus proofreading balances genome stability with viral fitness, provides a platform for studying reduced replication fidelity's effects on viral evolution and antiviral sensitivity, and may guide antiviral strategies targeting coronavirus proofreading.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in vitro and may not fully represent in vivo conditions; however, the use of direct biochemical assays and reverse genetics provides high confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether SARS-CoV-2 can tolerate impaired proofreading activity by its ExoN enzyme. Using biochemical assays and reverse genetics, the researchers found that partial impairment of ExoN activity is possible but requires a minimal activity threshold for viral viability. Mutants with reduced proofreading (D90A/E92A) exhibited a mutator phenotype with increased genome-wide mutations and reduced replication, while more severe defects (K9E) prevented virus recovery. These findings clarify how coronavirus proofreading balances genome stability and viral fitness, providing insights for antiviral strategies targeting this mechanism.

title: Intranasal SARS-CoV-2 vaccine boosting alters immune imprinting and B cell repertoire 2331448

analysis.research_question_and_background: Immune imprinting limits variant-specific de novo immune responses to subsequent related antigens, and strategies like changing dosage and interval have had limited success in enhancing variant-specific immunity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: C57BL/6 mice were primed intramuscularly with mRNA-1273 and heterologously boosted intramuscularly with a chimpanzee adenoviral-vectored vaccine against XBB.1.5 spike.
analysis.methods: Serum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid were analysed for cross-reactive and strain-specific spike-binding IgG/IgA, neutralizing activity was assessed using pseudovirus neutralization assays, and cross-reactive and strain-specific spike-binding memory B cells in draining lymph nodes were quantified.
analysis.main_results: Intranasal boosting with ChAd-SARS-CoV-2-S against XBB.1.5 spike induced higher fractions of XBB.1.5-specific serum IgG and BALF IgA with greater neutralizing activity and increased XBB.1.5-specific memory B cells in draining lymph nodes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Intranasal boosting promotes greater variant-specific response at both the serum and cellular levels than intramuscular boosting, and ongoing B cell repertoire and monoclonal antibody analyses will provide mechanistic insight into how vaccination route reshapes clonal selection and maturation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform rational vaccination design by demonstrating that intranasal boosting can overcome immune imprinting and enhance variant-specific immunity, which is crucial for developing more effective COVID-19 vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate as the study was conducted in mice, and ongoing analyses are needed to fully understand the mechanisms; however, the results provide promising insights for vaccine development.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how intranasal SARS-CoV-2 vaccine boosting alters immune imprinting and B cell repertoire. Immune imprinting limits variant-specific responses, and traditional strategies have been ineffective. The researchers primed mice with mRNA-1273 and boosted them intranasally with a chimpanzee adenoviral-vectored vaccine against XBB.1.5 spike. They found that intranasal boosting induced higher levels of XBB.1.5-specific serum IgG, BALF IgA, and neutralizing activity, along with increased XBB.1.5-specific memory B cells in draining lymph nodes. This demonstrates that intranasal boosting promotes greater variant-specific responses than intramuscular boosting. Ongoing analyses of B cell repertoires and monoclonal antibodies will provide further mechanistic insights. These findings are significant for designing more effective vaccines that can overcome immune imprinting.

title: Prevalence and Determinants of Hospital-Acquired Infections in Intensive Care Units Before and After the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Retrospective Descriptive Surveillance Study at a Tertiary Care Hospital in Iran.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and determinants of hospital-acquired infections (HAIs) in intensive care units (ICUs) before and after the COVID-19 pandemic, as HAIs cause significant morbidity, mortality, and costs.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective descriptive-analytical study was conducted on ICU patients admitted to Taleghani Hospital, Kermanshah, Iran, between 2019 and 2020. The study compared HAI prevalence, types, and causative agents in an Iranian tertiary hospital before and after the pandemic.
analysis.methods: Demographic, clinical, and microbiological data were collected from hospital records. Associations between categorical variables were assessed using Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, and continuous non-normally distributed variables were compared using the Mann–Whitney U test, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant.
analysis.main_results: Among 1778 ICU admissions, 301 cases of HAIs were identified, yielding an overall prevalence of 16.9%. The prevalence decreased from 131/718 (18.2%) in 2019 to 170/1060 (16.0%) in 2020. While VAE and pneumonia decreased in 2020, UTIs and BSIs increased.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that despite strengthened infection control during the pandemic, HAIs, particularly Gram-negative infections and VAE, remain prevalent in ICUs. The study provides novel insights into the changing patterns of HAIs during the pandemic.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for continuous surveillance and targeted interventions to reduce the burden of HAIs in ICUs, especially in the context of the ongoing pandemic.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on hospital records, which may introduce bias. The evidence strength is moderate, as the results are based on observational data and statistical associations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence and determinants of hospital-acquired infections (HAIs) in intensive care units (ICUs) in an Iranian tertiary hospital before and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The research aimed to understand how the pandemic affected HAI patterns, as HAIs are a significant cause of morbidity, mortality, and costs. A retrospective descriptive-analytical study was conducted on ICU patients admitted between 2019 and 2020, collecting demographic, clinical, and microbiological data. Statistical analyses were used to assess associations between infection occurrence and factors such as gender, ICU ward, and Gram-negative bacterial infections. The study found that overall HAI prevalence decreased slightly from 18.2% in 2019 to 16.0% in 2020, but there were shifts in infection types, with an increase in urinary tract infections (UTIs) and bloodstream infections (BSIs) in 2020. The authors concluded that HAIs, particularly Gram-negative infections and ventilator-associated events (VAE), remain prevalent in ICUs despite pandemic-related infection control measures. The findings emphasize the importance of ongoing surveillance and targeted interventions to mitigate the burden of HAIs in critical care settings.

title: Persistent SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein in Vasculitic Skin Lesions after Infection or mRNA Vaccination: A Retrospective Case control Immunofluorescence Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Vasculitic skin lesions have been reported in association with both SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination, but whether viral proteins persist in lesional vessels beyond the acute phase remains unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective case-control study includes 9 patients with persistent or delayed-onset vasculitic skin lesions following COVID-19 infection (n=4) or mRNA vaccination (n=5), with prepandemic leukocytoclastic vasculitis (n=3) and healthy postinfection/postvaccination skin (n=3) serving as controls.
analysis.methods: Skin biopsies were analysed using immunofluorescence for SARS-CoV-2 spike protein.
analysis.main_results: Spike protein was detected in vascular endothelial cells of all 9 patients with COVID-19- or vaccine-associated vasculitis, but staining was absent in all prepandemic vasculitis and healthy control samples.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings suggest that retained viral proteins may contribute to prolonged or delayed-onset vasculitic skin manifestations, demonstrating that SARS-CoV-2 spike protein can persist in endothelial cells of vasculitic skin lesions weeks to months after COVID-19 infection or mRNA vaccination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides evidence for a potential mechanism underlying persistent vasculitic skin manifestations after SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination, which may inform future diagnostic approaches and therapeutic strategies for such cases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Further studies are needed to clarify the mechanisms underlying spike persistence and its clinical significance; the evidence strength is moderate due to the small sample size and retrospective design.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective case-control study investigated the presence of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in vasculitic skin lesions following infection or vaccination. Nine patients with persistent or delayed-onset vasculitis (4 post-infection, 5 post-vaccination) were compared with controls (3 prepandemic vasculitis, 3 healthy skin). Immunofluorescence analysis revealed spike protein in all 9 patients but none of the controls. Histopathology showed typical leukocytoclastic vasculitis without viral cytopathic changes. The findings suggest that persistent spike protein may contribute to prolonged vasculitic manifestations, providing a potential mechanism for these clinical observations. However, the small sample size and retrospective design limit the strength of the evidence.

title: Seroprevalence and risk factors for SARS-CoV-2 infection among unvaccinated adults in a rural community in South-East Nigeria during the Omicron era: a community-based cross-sectional study

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the seroprevalence and risk factors for SARS-CoV-2 infection among unvaccinated adults in a rural community in South-East Nigeria during the Omicron era, addressing the lack of population-based data on SARS-CoV-2 exposure in sub-Saharan Africa.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A community-based cross-sectional study of 252 consenting unvaccinated adults was conducted from March 11 to June 12, 2022, in Enugu State, southeastern Nigeria. Thirty-nine (15.48%) out of 252 participants had both SARS-CoV-2 IgG and IgM antibodies.
analysis.methods: Each participant was tested for SARS-CoV-2 IgM and IgG antibodies using the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to determine factors independently associated with SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity.
analysis.main_results: The seroprevalence of SARS-CoV-2 (IgG or IgM) was 67.90%. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that healthcare workers had significantly higher odds of SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity than non-healthcare workers (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 3.83, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.52–9.66; P = 0.004).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The predominance of SARS-CoV-2 IgG over IgM antibodies suggests that most infections occurred before sample collection and is consistent with declining community transmission during the study period.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Serological evidence of SARS-CoV-2 infection was observed in approximately two out of every three unvaccinated adults, indicating widespread previous exposure through natural infection in the study population by the first half of 2022.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: A P-value of < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. The study was conducted in a single rural community, which may limit generalisability.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the seroprevalence and risk factors for SARS-CoV-2 infection among unvaccinated adults in a rural community in South-East Nigeria during the Omicron era. A cross-sectional design was used, involving 252 participants, with antibody testing via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The results showed a seroprevalence of 67.90%, with healthcare workers having significantly higher odds of seropositivity. The findings suggest widespread natural exposure to SARS-CoV-2 and declining community transmission. The study highlights the importance of infection prevention measures for healthcare workers. However, the single rural setting may limit generalisability, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study concludes that a single METTL3-dependent m6A methylation event in the 5′-UTR of SARS-CoV-2 regulates the rate of translation initiation. By testing thiol molecules, the study demonstrates their ability to restore glutathione balance and inhibit the AP-1 pathway, thereby reducing inflammation and viral replication. These findings suggest that targeting redox-sensitive factors could be a promising therapeutic approach for managing SARS-CoV-2 infections. However, the study is limited to in vitro models, which may restrict the applicability of the results to clinical settings. The evidence is strong and directly supports the proposed mechanisms, indicating a moderate confidence level in the findings.

title: Determinants of seasonal influenza and COVID-19 vaccine uptake in high-risk individuals in northern Sweden.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify the remaining vaccination barriers in high-income countries for seasonal influenza and COVID-19 vaccines in high-risk individuals. The background highlights that these vaccines prevent disease, disability, and death, yet vaccine coverage remains suboptimal.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study recruited patients seeking emergency department care at a hospital in northern Sweden. It included 600 patients, of whom 450 were eligible for both influenza and COVID-19 vaccines.
analysis.methods: Logistic regression was used to calculate odds ratios (OR) and adjusted odds ratios (aOR) for determinants associated with influenza and COVID-19 vaccination. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and medical records, and linked with community-level determinants from national registers.
analysis.main_results: Among eligible individuals, influenza vaccine coverage was 52.0% and COVID-19 vaccine coverage was 54.2%. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that vaccine uptake for influenza and COVID-19 was primarily associated with individual-level determinants, whereas community-level determinants showed little impact. This finding highlights the importance of addressing individual factors in improving vaccination rates.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted communication strategies and harmonized eligibility criteria to improve vaccination rates among high-risk individuals. They also suggest that community-level interventions may have limited influence on vaccine uptake.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single hospital in northern Sweden, which may affect generalisability. The evidence strength is moderate, as the results are based on a single setting and may not represent broader populations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the determinants of seasonal influenza and COVID-19 vaccine uptake among high-risk individuals in northern Sweden. It highlights that vaccine coverage remains suboptimal despite the known benefits of vaccination. The research design involved recruiting patients from an emergency department and collecting data through interviews and medical records. Logistic regression was used to analyze individual-level determinants, revealing that factors such as male sex, younger age, smoking, reduced independence, and age-only eligibility were associated with lower uptake. Community-level determinants had limited influence. The authors suggest that targeted communication and harmonized eligibility criteria could help overcome vaccination barriers. The study's findings have implications for improving vaccination rates in high-risk groups but are limited by their focus on a single setting, which may restrict generalisability.

title: Low dosage of a novel SARS-COV-2 mRNA-VLP vaccine elicits equivalent cell-mediated immunity to a licensed mRNA vaccine 2260043

analysis.research_question_and_background: mRNA-encoded virus-like particles (VLPs) are an emerging advancement in vaccine technology, enabling the self-assembly of viral antigens into structures that closely resemble native viruses. This innovative approach to conventional mRNA vaccination may boost vaccine-induced adaptive immune responses and allow for reduced dosing.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The phase 1 clinical study ARTEMIS-C was conducted to assess cellular immunogenicity in adults aged 18—64 years and ≥65 years following administration of AZD6563 (5 μg or 10 μg) or the licensed BNT162b2 XBB.1.5 mRNA vaccine (30 μg).
analysis.methods: To evaluate this technology, we developed AZD6563, an mRNA VLP vaccine targeting the COVID-19 XBB1.5 spike variant. The study assessed spike-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses and functional analysis of cytokine production profiles.
analysis.main_results: AZD6563 drove spike-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses comparable to those elicited by higher dose of BNT162b2. Functional analysis revealed similar cytokine production profiles across groups; however, the 10μg dose of AZD6563 led to higher TCR diversity within the ≥65-year cohort. Expansion of spike-specific B cells was most pronounced in the AZD6563 10μg group, with marked increases in cross-reactive XBB.1.5 spike-specific B cells that also recognized Omicron BA.4/5 and ancestral SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Collectively, these results demonstrate that AZD6563, at reduced doses, matches the cellular immunogenicity of BNT162b2 while enhancing B cell cross-reactivity and TCR diversity in older adults, supporting its potential as a next-generation COVID-19 vaccine candidate.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that AZD6563 could offer a more efficient vaccination strategy with lower doses while maintaining robust immune responses and potentially broader protection against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, which could improve vaccine accessibility and coverage.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was a phase 1 clinical trial with a limited sample size, and further research is needed to evaluate long-term immunity and efficacy in larger populations. Despite these limitations, the evidence strength is moderate due to the well-controlled design and direct comparison with a licensed vaccine.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated AZD6563, an mRNA virus-like particle (VLP) vaccine targeting the COVID-19 XBB1.5 spike variant, in a phase 1 clinical trial (ARTEMIS-C) comparing it to the licensed BNT162b2 mRNA vaccine. Results showed that AZD6563 at reduced doses (5μg or 10μg) elicited comparable spike-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses to the higher dose of BNT162b2 (30μg). The 10μg dose of AZD6563 also demonstrated higher TCR diversity in older adults and enhanced expansion of cross-reactive B cells recognizing multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants. These findings support AZD6563 as a promising next-generation COVID-19 vaccine candidate with potential advantages in dose-sparing and broader variant coverage.

title: Discordant Anti-SARS-COV-2 IgA Responses In Blood, Saliva, and Tears 2261177

analysis.research_question_and_background: To determine whether anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgA responses in blood reflected the expression of anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgA in mucosal tissues, anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgA antibodies in blood plasma, tears and saliva were measured before and after SARS-CoV-2 exposure or COVID-19 vaccination.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Blood plasma was available from fourteen individuals before and after SARS-CoV-2 exposure or COVID-19 vaccination, with a larger cohort of 39 participants who were anti-SARS-CoV-2 RBD IgG positive.
analysis.methods: Anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgA antibodies in blood plasma, tears and saliva were measured by indirect ELISA using Wuhan or Omicron RBD-coated plates, with specimens added at specific dilutions and a monoclonal antibody standard for concentration determination.
analysis.main_results: Seroconversion for anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies was observed in all individuals, but only six of fourteen (43%) demonstrated anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgA antibodies; in the larger cohort, 16 (41%), 9 (23%), and 11 (28%) were positive for anti-SARS-CoV-2 RBD IgA in blood, saliva and tears respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgA responses in blood, tears, and saliva are variable with discordant responses in blood and mucosal tissues, and equivalent antibody responses in tears of both eyes suggest equal seeding of both lacrimal glands by antibody-producing B cells.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform that mucosal IgA responses may not reliably be predicted by blood IgA levels, which has implications for surveillance, vaccination strategies, and understanding mucosal immunity against SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the small sample size and the abstract-only nature of the study, which limits detailed assessment of generalizability and potential biases.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgA responses in blood reflected mucosal tissue expression by measuring IgA in blood plasma, tears, and saliva before and after SARS-CoV-2 exposure or vaccination. Results showed that while all 14 individuals seroconverted for IgG, only 43% had detectable IgA in blood. In a larger cohort of 39 IgG-positive individuals, 41% had blood IgA, 23% had saliva IgA, and 28% had tears IgA. Notably, 44% of blood IgA-positive individuals were also positive in saliva or tears, while 30% of blood IgA-negative individuals were positive in mucosal samples. The authors concluded that IgA responses are discordant between blood and mucosal tissues, with implications for understanding mucosal immunity and vaccination strategies.

title: SARS-CoV-2 mRNA Vaccination Induces Neutralizing Antibodies and Type I IFN Changes in People Living With HIV.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study examined changes in anti-Spike antibodies and type I interferon following the BNT162b2 vaccine in people living with HIV (PLWH) and analyzed the impact of demographic and immunological factors.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In total, 75 PLWH and 28 healthy donors were followed at baseline (T0), at the second dose (T1), after the second dose (T2), and more than 1 year later (T3).
analysis.methods: Anti-S antibodies were assessed by chemiluminescence and vesicular stomatitis virus-based pseudo virus-neutralization assay, while IFN-α2, IFN-β, and IFN-ω mRNA levels were measured by RT-Real Time PCR.
analysis.main_results: PLWH showed an increase in anti-S Immunoglobulin G levels comparable to healthy donors (p < 0.001) and an induction of anti-S neutralizing antibodies (p < 0.014 for T2 vs.). IFN-I gene expression showed temporal changes, with a decrease at T2 (p < 0.01) and a subsequent increase at T3 (p < 0.001, for IFN-α2 and IFN-ω). A multivariable model revealed no overall change in the IFN-I response over time, except for IFN-β, which was lower at T3 than at T1 (p = 0.032).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These results suggest that mRNA vaccination can elicit an effective anti-S response and modulate the IFN-β gene expression in PLWH, with CD4+ T cell count being a key determinant of vaccine-induced changes in IFN.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform vaccine strategies for PLWH, demonstrating effective antibody responses and highlighting the role of CD4+ T cell count in modulating interferon responses, which may impact long-term vaccine efficacy and immune monitoring.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational design and limited sample size, though the longitudinal assessment and multivariable analysis provide robust insights into vaccine responses in PLWH.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the immune response to BNT162b2 mRNA vaccination in 75 people living with HIV (PLWH) and 28 healthy donors over multiple time points. Results showed comparable anti-S IgG increases and neutralizing antibody induction in PLWH versus healthy donors, with type I interferon (IFN-I) gene expression exhibiting temporal changes. CD4+ T cell count was positively correlated with IFN-I response, while age, gender, and baseline IFN-I levels did not affect antibody production. The findings suggest effective vaccine responses in PLWH, with CD4+ T cell count as a key determinant of IFN modulation, informing vaccination strategies for this population.

title: Factors Associated With Job Precariousness and Material Deprivation, and Their Association With Mental Health During the COVID-19 Pandemic.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed how pre-existing mental health conditions influenced socio-economic adversity during the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic and whether resilience moderated mental health changes. It aimed to identify whether anxiety, depression, or suicide-related symptoms predicted job precariousness and material deprivation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A nationally representative longitudinal cohort of Spanish adults was assessed at two time points: November 2019 (pre-pandemic) and November–December 2020 (during the pandemic). Major depressive episode, generalized anxiety disorder, and suicidal thoughts and behaviors were measured at baseline, while job precariousness and material deprivation were evaluated at follow-up.
analysis.methods: Weighted multivariable regression models were used to test associations between pre-pandemic mental health conditions and subsequent socio-economic adversity, as well as the impact of adversity on changes in mental health symptoms. Resilience was examined as an interaction term in these models.
analysis.main_results: Pre-pandemic generalized anxiety disorder and suicidal thoughts and behaviors were associated with higher odds of job precariousness during the pandemic, whereas major depressive episode was not significant after adjustment. Job precariousness was linked to small reductions in depressive, anxiety, and suicidal thoughts and behaviors symptoms, while material deprivation was associated with increased depressive symptoms. Higher resilience attenuated the association between deprivation and depression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that pre-existing anxiety and suicide-related symptoms may identify individuals at greater risk of job precariousness during socio-economic shocks. They highlighted the potential protective role of resilience in mitigating the adverse mental health effects of material deprivation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that addressing material deprivation and strengthening resilience could reduce downstream depressive burden during crises. They also imply that mental health screening may help identify individuals at risk of socio-economic adversity in pandemic contexts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relied on self-reported measures of mental health and socio-economic adversity, which may introduce bias. The longitudinal design and nationally representative sampling strengthen the evidence, but generalizability to other contexts remains uncertain.

analysis.summary_en: This study examined how pre-existing mental health conditions influenced socio-economic adversity during the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic in a nationally representative cohort of Spanish adults. Using weighted multivariable regression models, the authors found that generalized anxiety disorder and suicidal thoughts and behaviors at baseline were associated with higher odds of job precariousness during the pandemic, while major depressive episode was not significant after adjustment. Job precariousness was linked to small reductions in mental health symptoms, whereas material deprivation was associated with increased depressive symptoms. Higher resilience attenuated the adverse mental health effects of deprivation. The authors concluded that pre-existing anxiety and suicide-related symptoms may identify individuals at greater risk of job precariousness during socio-economic shocks and emphasized the potential protective role of resilience in mitigating depressive burden during crises.

title: Anti-PEG Antibodies From mRNA COVID-19 Vaccines Affect In Vitro Measurements of Pegylated Drug Levels.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to address the scientific problem of whether anti-PEG antibodies generated by mRNA-based SARS-CoV-2 vaccines could interfere with in vitro measurements of pegylated drug levels. The objective was to investigate this potential interference.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study assessed the presence of anti-PEG antibodies in human serum following SARS-CoV-2 vaccination, comparing vaccine recipients to control samples. The study included individuals who received the mRNA-1273 vaccine and those who received other vaccines such as BNT162b2 or Ad26.COV2.S.
analysis.methods: The study measured anti-PEG antibody levels in serum samples collected pre- and post-vaccination using bioanalytical assays. It also evaluated the effect of these antibodies on the detection of pegfilgrastim, a pegylated drug, in serum samples.
analysis.main_results: Elevated anti-PEG antibody titers with prolonged prevalence were detected in individuals who received the mRNA-1273 vaccine compared to control samples. Anti-PEG antibody levels were approximately 10-fold higher post-vaccination compared to pre-vaccination in approximately 33% of assessed mRNA-1273 vaccine recipients.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that anti-PEG antibodies can interfere with bioanalytical assays used for pharmacokinetic drug measurement, which has implications for the development and comparability of pegylated pharmaceutical products.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results caution against the potential for anti-PEG antibodies to affect the accuracy of drug level assessments in individuals vaccinated with mRNA-based SARS-CoV-2 vaccines, which is important for drug development and clinical monitoring.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro measurements and does not account for clinical or real-world implications. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a single study with a specific focus on antibody levels and drug detection.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates whether anti-PEG antibodies generated by mRNA-based SARS-CoV-2 vaccines could interfere with in vitro measurements of pegylated drug levels. It finds that individuals who received the mRNA-1273 vaccine had elevated anti-PEG antibody titers compared to control samples, with levels approximately 10-fold higher post-vaccination in about 33% of recipients. The study also shows that serum from individuals with elevated anti-PEG antibodies typically showed decreased detection of the pegylated drug, pegfilgrastim. These findings highlight the potential for anti-PEG antibodies to affect bioanalytical assays used for drug measurement, which has implications for the development of pegylated pharmaceutical products. The study is limited to in vitro settings and does not account for clinical relevance, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Thrombotic and cerebrovascular events following SARS-CoV-2 vaccination: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses

analysis.scope_and_question: This umbrella review examines thrombotic and cerebrovascular events following SARS-CoV-2 vaccination, focusing on acute ischemic stroke and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis across different vaccine platforms.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes evidence from 19 systematic reviews and meta-analyses, with methodological quality assessed using AMSTAR-2. Findings were categorized by outcome and vaccine platform.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Evidence consistently shows thrombotic and cerebrovascular events after vaccination are rare. mRNA vaccines (BNT162b2, mRNA-1273) were not associated with increased risk beyond background rates. Adenoviral vector vaccines (ChAdOx1 nCoV-19, Ad26.COV2.S) were linked to rare vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia, primarily presenting as cerebral venous sinus thrombosis in younger adults. Whole-virus vaccines showed limited evidence without consistent safety concerns.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies limited evidence for whole-virus vaccines and highlights the need for ongoing surveillance to monitor rare thrombotic events, particularly for adenoviral vector vaccines in younger populations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Vaccination benefits outweigh risks, emphasizing the importance of continued surveillance and transparent communication about rare adverse events.

analysis.summary_en: This umbrella review synthesizes evidence from 19 systematic reviews and meta-analyses on thrombotic and cerebrovascular events after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. It finds these events are rare, with mRNA vaccines showing no increased risk beyond background rates. Adenoviral vector vaccines are linked to rare immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia, primarily as cerebral venous sinus thrombosis in younger adults. Whole-virus vaccines have limited evidence without consistent safety concerns. The review concludes vaccination benefits outweigh risks, highlighting the need for ongoing surveillance and transparent communication.
